zakkur-stele: The Zakkur Stele, an Aramaic inscription of King Zakkur of Hamath and Lu'ash (about 800 BC), which names Hadrach as Hazrak
jerome-matthew-27: Jerome, Commentary on Matthew, book 4, on Matthew 27:9-10, in Complete Works of Saint Jerome, vol. 7, ed. J.-P. Migne (Garnier, Paris, 1865)
arrian-anabasis-2: Arrian, The Anabasis of Alexander, book 2 (Tyre 2.16-24; Gaza 2.25-27), English translation by E. J. Chinnock
sifre-deuteronomy: Sifre Deuteronomy (rabbinic midrash), Pisqa 1, English text as published on Sefaria
rashi-zechariah: Rashi (Solomon ben Isaac), commentary on Zechariah 12:10-11, English text as published on Sefaria
baptist-faith-message-2000-last-things: The Baptist Faith and Message (Southern Baptist Convention, 2000), article 10, "Last Things"
targum-jonathan-zech-9-14-sefaria: Targum Jonathan (Aramaic translation of the Prophets) on Zechariah 12:10-11 and 14:21, Aramaic text on Sefaria (sefaria.org/Targum_Jonathan_on_Zechariah)
christian-thinktank-matt-27-9: Glenn Miller, "Where was the Judas quote from, actually?" (christian-thinktank.com), which collects the views of Keener, Kaiser and others, Beale and Carson, Turner and Bock, and Barbieri
freebiblecommentary-matt-27-9: Free Bible Commentary, "Special Topic: Matthew 27:9" (freebiblecommentary.org), which lists nine views and who holds them
gaebelein-zech-12-14: Arno C. Gaebelein, Gaebelein's Annotated Bible, comments on Zechariah 12 and 14 (read on biblehub.com)
